representation_warning: Map pins approximate regions or representative tissue locations. They are not receptor-density measurements, expression quantification, or anatomical diagnostics.
medical_boundary: Evidence about receptor location and experimental pathways does not establish treatment benefits, dosing, safety or restoration of homeostasis.

regions.label: Brain
regions.intro: The cerebral map is a schematic locator. CB1 distribution is heterogeneous across neurons and brain regions; this is not a receptor density heatmap.

receptors.summary: CB1 is abundant at many presynaptic neuronal terminals and contributes to locally regulated neurotransmitter release.
receptors.cell_context: Neural circuits in cortex, hippocampus, basal ganglia and cerebellum; regional densities differ.
pathway: Postsynaptic activity can promote local 2-AG production in some synapses.
2-AG activates presynaptic CB1 signaling.
Presynaptic transmitter release probability can fall.
receptors.model: Cellular physiology and nervous-system localization from human and preclinical studies.
receptors.boundary: This local feedback example does not show that cannabis improves brain function, memory, mood or sleep.

receptors.summary: CB2 has been reported in selected neural and neuroimmune contexts, particularly under injury or inflammation; baseline human brain expression remains method- and cell-dependent.
receptors.cell_context: Microglia and selected neural populations in experimental studies; not uniformly present across brain cells.
pathway: Experimental injury or inflammatory conditions can change CB2 expression in neuroimmune cells.
CB2-linked signaling can modulate studied neuroimmune responses.
receptors.model: Mostly cellular and animal models with limited human localization data.
receptors.boundary: Do not infer a general CB2 brain-wide distribution or a proven human neuroprotective treatment.

regions.label: Peripheral nerves
regions.intro: Schematic placement on a leg represents sensory pathways rather than one localized 'nerve organ'.

receptors.summary: CB1-related signaling has been identified along nociceptive circuitry, including primary afferents and spinal dorsal-horn pathways.
receptors.cell_context: Primary sensory neurons, peripheral nerve endings and spinal sensory processing in studied models.
pathway: Sensory input reaches peripheral neurons and the spinal cord.
Local endocannabinoid–CB1 mechanisms can alter synaptic nociceptive transmission in experimental preparations.
receptors.model: Preclinical pain physiology and receptor localization; species and experimental context matter.
receptors.boundary: Animal nociception is not evidence that a cannabis product relieves a human patient's pain.

regions.label: Gut
regions.system: Enteric nervous system and intestinal immune tissue
regions.intro: A gut-region marker groups enteric nerves, epithelial tissues and immune compartments; it does not imply every gut cell carries both receptors.

receptors.summary: CB1 is described in enteric neuronal circuits and some intestinal non-neuronal cell populations.
receptors.cell_context: Myenteric and submucosal enteric neurons; selected epithelial or endocrine compartments.
pathway: Local endocannabinoid signaling engages CB1 on relevant enteric neurons.
Presynaptic neurotransmitter release and intestinal motility can be modulated in studied systems.
receptors.model: Cellular, animal and human gastrointestinal distribution/physiology literature.
receptors.boundary: Receptor involvement in motility does not establish cannabis as safe or effective for IBS, nausea or inflammatory bowel disease.

receptors.summary: CB2 is reported in intestinal immune cells and some enteric compartments, with expression influenced by inflammation.
receptors.cell_context: Intestinal immune cells and model-dependent enteric/epithelial populations.
pathway: Inflammatory context can change local immune signaling and receptor expression.
CB2-associated pathways can alter immune mediator responses in experimental gut systems.
receptors.model: Gastrointestinal cellular and animal studies with some human tissue observations.
receptors.boundary: A plausible immunological mechanism is not clinical evidence that a cannabis product treats inflammatory bowel disease.

regions.label: Immune tissues
regions.system: Immune cells, spleen and lymphoid organs
regions.intro: The marker approximates the splenic/lymphoid region, but mobile immune cells circulate throughout the body.

receptors.summary: CB2 has comparatively prominent expression in many immune-cell populations and lymphoid tissues; levels vary with cell type and activation.
receptors.cell_context: B and T lymphocytes, macrophages and tissues such as spleen and thymus, depending on study.
pathway: An immune cell expresses CB2 in a particular context.
Receptor-linked signaling can alter downstream immune mediator pathways in experimental systems.
receptors.model: Human tissue localization, cellular studies and animal immune-signaling models.
receptors.boundary: This does not establish that consuming cannabis 'boosts immunity', safely suppresses inflammation or treats autoimmune disease.

regions.label: Liver
regions.intro: Hepatic expression is context-sensitive; this map does not assign a receptor density to liver tissue.

receptors.summary: Peripheral CB1 signaling has been studied in liver metabolism and energy-balance pathways.
receptors.cell_context: Hepatic cell populations and associated metabolic regulation in experimental and translational studies.
pathway: Local peripheral ECS signals can engage hepatic CB1-related pathways.
Downstream metabolic effects vary across models and physiological states.
receptors.model: Mixed human/animal tissue-expression and metabolic mechanism literature.
receptors.boundary: Not evidence that cannabis consumption cleanses the liver, treats fatty liver disease or improves metabolism.

regions.label: Adipose tissue
regions.intro: The abdominal placement is illustrative. Fat tissue is distributed throughout the body and is biologically heterogeneous.

receptors.summary: CB1 is reported in adipose and other peripheral metabolic tissues, which participate in energy-balance signaling.
receptors.cell_context: Adipocytes and metabolic regulatory contexts, not a universal expression level for all fat depots.
pathway: Endocannabinoid signaling can engage local CB1 pathways in studied metabolic tissues.
Metabolic and endocrine responses depend on physiological context and study model.
receptors.model: Human and animal metabolic physiology reviews and cell studies.
receptors.boundary: Receptor presence does not show that cannabis improves weight, appetite regulation or insulin sensitivity.

regions.label: Skin
regions.system: Cutaneous cells, nerves and immune responses
regions.intro: The arm location represents distributed skin, hair follicles, glands and cutaneous nerves, not an isolated skin organ.

receptors.summary: CB1 is described in several skin compartments including keratinocytes, nerves and skin appendages.
receptors.cell_context: Keratinocytes, hair follicles, cutaneous nerves and other skin-cell subtypes.
pathway: Endogenous lipids and local skin cells participate in cutaneous ECS signaling.
CB1-associated effects on barrier, sensory or cellular processes depend on experimental context.
receptors.model: Human skin-cell work and preclinical dermatology research.
receptors.boundary: Skin receptor expression is not evidence of efficacy for cannabis creams, eczema, psoriasis or wound healing.

receptors.summary: CB2 has been reported in skin immune populations and other cutaneous cell compartments.
receptors.cell_context: Immune cells, keratinocytes and skin appendages; distribution differs by cell type.
pathway: Local immunological and tissue cues can engage cutaneous CB2-linked signaling.
Experimental responses involve multiple receptors and cell types, not only CB2.
receptors.model: Human skin expression and experimental dermatology studies.
receptors.boundary: Mechanistic skin biology does not establish safe or effective clinical use of topical cannabis preparations.
